page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is an entry-level burstable instance driven by a single physical Intel Xeon 8269CY CPU core running at 2.5 GHz, providing 2 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading on a KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 instruction set extensions. It carries no attached local SSD storage, no dedicated GPUs, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and operates at a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect its resource-constrained and burstable nature. In stress-ng CPU testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1161.28 and a multi-core score of 2371.48, placing it in low performance categories. PassMark evaluation recorded a CPU score of 3062.61 and a memory score of 1168.91. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrated uncached large-block read speeds of 22.38 GB/sec and write speeds of 19.14 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 2.58 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 2.61 million operations per second in Redis SET tasks, while small model LLM text generation reached 43.21 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the burstable CPU allocation and absence of dedicated local storage offer an economical hardware profile for non-continuous or low-intensity background workloads. However, sustained compute-heavy demands will quickly exhaust CPU credits, leading to throttled processing. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, basic web hosting, small internal utilities, continuous integration agents with intermittent build patterns, or development and testing environments where continuous CPU utilization is unnecessary.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable virtual server built on a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 1 physical core, 2 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture and AVX-512 support, this instance lacks local storage, GPUs, and baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate low processing and memory capabilities, registering 1161.28 in stress-ng single-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 3062.61, and 22.38 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Application throughput reached 2.58 GB/sec for static web serving and 2.61 million operations per second for Redis SET operations. Due to its burstable vCPU baseline and economical resource footprint, the instance provides cost efficiency for intermittent workloads but exhibits sharp trade-offs under sustained computation. It is recommended for low-concurrency web hosting, microservices, testing environments, and periodic background tasks.
